newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian girl, 12, dies of drug overdose.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian girl, 12, dies of drug overdose.

text.p: A 12-year-old girl was found dead of a drug overdose in the streets of Rio de Janeiro's neighbouring city of Niteroi, a police spokesman said on Wednesday.

Police found Marcela Lima dos Santos dressed in her school uniform dead in front of a pharmacy early on Tuesday after a porter at one of the nearby apartment buildings alerted police, the spokesman said.
"We believe she died of an overdose of drugs, but we don't know yet what type of drug," he said. "A large amount of pills were found in her stomach."

The police spokesman denied press reports claiming that police had ignored several telephone calls during the night by different people asking police to help the girl who was writhing in pain for 1 1/2 hours on the pavement.
He said there had been only one phone call advising police that the girl had been found dead in front of the pharmacy.

A recent study conducted by Rio de Janeiro state university UERJ over three years found that the age at which students in Rio schools first experimented with drugs had dropped to 12 years as opposed to 14 years at the beginning of the decade.
Alcohol and cigarettes are the most common psychoactive substances used by school children, followed by solvents, tranquillisers, marijuana and cocaine, according to the study.
